subtitulo: Hedging a health claim so it survives
descripcion: Hedging is argumentative precision, not politeness. A hedged claim is harder to attack, easier to revise and more acceptable to an audience that does not share your view. English does this lexically and modally — there is no hedging tense. It lives in adverbs, modals, reporting structures and impersonal constructions.

filas: *there's some evidence that*, *as far as I can tell*, *on the numbers I've seen*
*it could be argued that*, *there's a case for*, *one reading is*
*I'd be careful about*, *I could be wrong*, *speaking outside my area*
*up to a point*, *in principle*, *at least for X*

ejemplos.texto: *That tends to be the case, though the data is thinner than people assume.*
*There's some evidence to suggest that offsets underperform their stated value.*
*I'd be careful about generalising from one grid.*
*It could be argued that the cost falls on the wrong people.*
*As far as I can tell, nobody has measured this properly.*

notas: *Would* is the single most productive device: *I'd say*, *I'd argue*, *I'd be careful about*.
One or two hedges per claim is the ceiling. Stacking destroys credibility.
Never hedge a verifiable number — it reads as evasive, not careful.

es.en: Spanish often states a limit plainly («eso no funciona»), and the literal that doesn't work sounds blunt in English. The equivalent English register is I don't think that's going to work.
es.es: El español suele expresar un límite de manera directa («eso no funciona»), y el literal «that doesn't work» suena brusco en inglés. El equivalente de registro natural es «I don't think that's going to work».

de.en: German softens a plain statement with particles («das funktioniert so wohl nicht»), but the particles disappear in translation and that doesn't work remains. English needs a lexical hedge instead: I don't think that's going to work.
de.de: Deutsch schwächt eine direkte Aussage mit Partikeln ab («das funktioniert so wohl nicht»). Bei der Übersetzung verschwinden sie und übrig bleibt «that doesn't work». Englisch braucht stattdessen eine lexikalische Abschwächung: «I don't think that's going to work».

it.en: «Non credo che funzioni» corresponds exactly to I don't think it'll work, with the negation in the same place. The hedge therefore transfers directly.
it.it: «Non credo che funzioni» corrisponde esattamente a «I don't think it'll work», con la negazione nello stesso punto. L'attenuazione si trasferisce quindi direttamente.

fr.en: «Je ne pense pas que ça marche» corresponds exactly to I don't think it'll work, with the negation in the same place. The hedge therefore transfers directly.
fr.fr: «Je ne pense pas que ça marche» correspond exactement à «I don't think it'll work», avec la négation au même endroit. L'atténuation se transfère donc directement.

pt.en: Portuguese often says «acho que isso não vai funcionar», with the negation in the second clause. English prefers it in the first: I don't think that's going to work.
pt.pt: O português costuma dizer «acho que isso não vai funcionar», com a negação na segunda oração. O inglês prefere colocá-la na primeira: «I don't think that's going to work».

errores: *Eventually* means 'in the end', not 'possibly', despite its look-alikes in other European languages.
*Maybe* sentence-initially reads tentative rather than considered. Prefer *perhaps* or *I'd say*.
Under-hedging, which reads as aggressive rather than confident.

es: «*Parece ser que*» rendered as *It seems to be that* instead of *It seems that*.
de: «*Es scheint so, als ob*» rendered as *It seems so as if* instead of *It looks as if*.
it: «*A quanto pare*» rendered as *At how much it seems* instead of *Apparently*.
fr: «*À ce qu'il paraît*» rendered as *At what it appears* instead of *Apparently*.
pt: «*Pelos vistos*» rendered as *By the seen* instead of *Apparently*.

vocabulario.item: the limit of what one can take

traducciones.de: Es gibt gewisse Hinweise darauf, dass…
traducciones.fr: Il y a des éléments indiquant que…
traducciones.it: Ci sono alcuni elementi che indicano che…

redemittel.expresion: As far as I can tell…
redemittel.funcion: marks the limits of what you know

traducciones.fr: Pour autant que je puisse en juger…

traducciones.de: Nach den Zahlen, die ich gesehen habe…
traducciones.fr: D’après les chiffres que j’ai vus…
traducciones.it: In base ai dati che ho visto…
traducciones.pt: Com base nos números que vi…

mision.consigna: Explain to a friend why you think preventive check-ups matter, without overstating the evidence.
requisitos: four different hedging devices (modal, adverb, reporting, impersonal)
no claim stronger than your evidence

microtareas.texto: Write three health claims you believe. Hedge each exactly as far as your evidence goes.
Find a claim online about *staying fit* and rewrite it honestly hedged.
Record 90 seconds: *Does exercise speed up how you recover from illness?* Hedge everything.

autochequeo: Six devices from four different types?
Any sentence with three or more hedges?
Did I hedge a verifiable number?
Is there at least one flat factual statement, to show I know the difference?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on hedging. (1) Mark each device and say whether it fits the claim and the register. (2) Mark where I asserted flatly and a C1 professional would have hedged. (3) Mark over-hedging and show the tighter version. (4) Did I hedge any verifiable fact? Do not rewrite the text.
